panels.description: Wide, full page width. The Travancore coast some months after the battle. A new laterite bastion rising above the beach, bamboo scaffolding lashed along its face, labourers hauling cut blocks up an earth ramp. On the finished parapet, Nair musketeers: bare-chested, white mundu hitched, hair in topknots, new flintlock muskets on their shoulders; NO red coats, NO blue coats, no hats. Beyond them, a flat bright sea with no sail on it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It had been some time since Colachel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Long enough for Batavia to send new instructions.

panels.description: A pepper market under palm-thatch awnings, sacks slumped open, a brass scale with coins in one pan. Yusuf Marakkar (Ibrahim's cousin, a coastal Muslim trader: leaner build, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, a sea captain's short coat; NO scar and NO turban, so he never reads as Ibrahim) leaning across a table piled with cloth, mid-anecdote, half-smiling, his eyes sliding sideways toward the street.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We heard of the envoys before we saw them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yusuf Marakkar always seemed to know a little more than he said.

panels.description: A temple mandapam at dusk, oil lamps on a brass stand. A plump man in a merchant's fine cloth, head bowed low before a Hindu ritual priest (V13 temple-priest face), pressing a single foreign silver coin into the offering tray as if glad to be rid of it. The priest's face unreadable.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men who had once taken Dutch bribes now feared they had backed the wrong god.

panels.description: Ramayyan's writing room, morning light through a wooden lattice. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) cross-legged on a mat among bundles of palm leaves, tapping a leaf with his iron stylus. Nagoji standing in the doorway, as Ananthan Pillai: BLACK hair in a Kerala topknot with only a first touch of grey at the temples (NOT the grey later-life figure on the sheet), NO turban, plain cream mundu with NO gold border and a shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife with the conch mark at his waist, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, the brand just above his left wrist. NO silver chain yet; it is fastened on him the morning of the audience.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They will come.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Not with drums, this time. With papers.

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width. The beach below the new bastion. A longboat run up on the sand, oars shipped, a plain pennant at the stern. Two Dutch envoys stepping ashore, hats in their hands rather than on their heads: the senior (fifties, heavy-lidded, grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, lace reduced to a thin trim at the cuff, black tricorne held to his chest) and the younger (twenties, thin, his own brown hair tied back, NO wig, brown coat, tricorne in hand). Neither wears the blue VOC soldier's coat. Behind them, Dutch scribes (European clerks, bareheaded, plain grey coats) wading through the shallows with thick bundles of paper tied in ribbon, held high above the surf. No drums. No soldiers.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They hoped paper could balance scales that guns had tipped.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The coastal hall: carved wooden pillars on laterite bases, a tiled roof on dark rafters, tall brass lamp stands. Marthanda Varma (V13 varma-v1 face; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare-chested, cream and gold cloth, gold necklaces) seated on his low platform, bare feet on a woven mat, his spear leaning within reach. Nagoji is the only STANDING figure beside the platform, close in on the king's right, as Ananthan Pillai: BLACK hair in a Kerala topknot with only a first touch of grey at the temples (NOT the grey later-life figure on the sheet), NO turban, plain cream mundu with NO gold border and a shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife with the conch mark at his waist, the heavy silver chain of office across his chest, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) seated cross-legged low at the foot of the platform with leaves and stylus. Ministers seated in the mid-ground along both sides, bareheaded, in white cloth, no chains. On the left, seated, Padmini Amma (fifties, thick black hair coiled at the nape, cotton sari, simple gold, long walking stick) with Revathi Bayi beside her (deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline; still a widow, so no tali). At the far end, the Dutch party only as backlit silhouettes in the glare of the doorway.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was no longer the mercenary observing from the pillars.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was the *Valia Karyakkar* of the Horse.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Nagoji's chest and shoulder: the cream shoulder cloth, the heavy silver chain of office lying across it, the ivory hilt of the conch-mark knife at the lower edge of the frame. At the top edge only, his clean-shaven chin and the end of his thick curled moustache.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Padmini Amma had fastened it around my neck that morning.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was a man with a *tharavadu* now, and that gave me a weight that mere steel could not.

panels.description: The senior envoy (fifties, heavy-lidded, grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, thin lace at the cuff, black tricorne held to his chest) walking up the hall toward us. His eyes slide sideways to Nagoji, who stands at the right edge of the frame, cropped at the shoulder (black topknot, NO turban, cream shoulder cloth, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin), and stay on the silver chain a beat too long. The younger envoy at his elbow (twenties, thin, anxious, his own brown hair tied back, NO wig, brown coat, tricorne in hand) follows his look.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They suspected the "Maratha" had found a permanent stall in this stable.

panels.description: Wide, shot from behind Lannoy's shoulder at the edge of the hall. Lannoy in the near foreground at frame right, back three-quarter view: tall, pale hair tied back, no wig, a WHITE cotton coat (not blue) over an open-collared European shirt, white mundu, a European sword at his side whose hilt is wrapped in local cloth. Two Nair palace guards (bare-chested, white mundu, sword and round shield) stand at ease beside him, paying him no special attention. Beyond him the two envoys have stopped in the aisle. The younger man's mouth is still open. The senior man's face has already smoothed over, and he dips a slight, stiff bow, tricorne against his chest.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: <Captain De Lannoy.>

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: <We were told...>

panels.description: Close on Lannoy: pale hair tied back, no wig, WHITE cotton coat over the open-collared shirt. Calm. Nothing given away.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: <You were told many things.>

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: <Some of them were true.>

panels.description: Lannoy (WHITE cotton coat, pale hair tied back) stepping back out of frame right, ceding the centre of the hall. The envoys turning to face the platform. Varma beyond them (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest), perfectly still, the smallest narrowing of the eyes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If the king felt any satisfaction at the sight of Dutchmen forced to greet one of their own as a subordinate in his court, he did not show it.

panels.description: The senior envoy bowing, tricorne pressed to his chest. A half step behind him the interpreter leans in, relaying: a younger local man standing empty-handed, with a coloured-border shoulder cloth and no palm leaves, so he never reads as Ramayyan.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: The Honourable Company conveys its formal regrets for the unfortunate conflict at Colachel.

panels.description: Varma (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; cream and gold, gold necklaces), head tilted a fraction, one hand resting on his knee.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Regrets.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You regret that your men died when they tried to land on my shore.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you regret sending them here at all?

panels.description: The envoy spreading his hands in the practised gesture of his trade. Behind him the Dutch scribes (bareheaded, plain grey coats) clutch their ribbon-tied bundles tighter.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: Circumstances were misjudged. We underestimated the strength and resolve of Travancore.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: We have been instructed to correct this error.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: By whose instruction?

panels.description: Padmini in the foreground, both hands folded on the head of her stick, speaking to no one in particular. The envoy small in the background, already beckoning a scribe forward.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: The Governor General and Council at Batavia.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: So far from this coast.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Yet their decisions wash up here like driftwood.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: The Company proposes a treaty.

panels.description: A Dutch scribe (European clerk, bareheaded, plain grey coat) stepping forward, offering a folded, ribbon-tied document with both hands. Ramayyan does not reach for it. He lifts two fingers, and his own young scribe (a youth in a white mundu, hair in a topknot) kneels at his side with a blank palm leaf and a stylus.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Read.

panels.description: Over Revathi's shoulder, seated, not rising: her profile in the near foreground (indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace). Mid-ground, the Dutch scribe reading from the unfolded paper, its lines faint marks with no legible writing. Beyond, the senior envoy's face turned toward her, his jaw tightening. He gives no answer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Recognition of Travancore's sovereignty. No new forts without consultation. Pepper at agreed prices. Suppression of piracy on the coast.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Who decides who is a pirate?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: In Velinadu, when we killed company men who broke their word, you called us pirates.

panels.description: Close on Lannoy at his pillar (pale hair tied back, WHITE cotton coat), arms folded. One corner of his mouth twitches. In the soft background, the Dutch scribe still reading.

copy.speaker: DUTCH SCRIBE (off)
copy.text: ...friendship and alliance, in the event of encroachment by any other European power.

panels.description: Wide and tall. Varma from a low angle (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest), leaning forward a fraction on the platform, the spear upright beside him; the envoy in the near foreground, back to us. Nagoji standing at the king's right (black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife at his waist, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin). Along both sides of the hall, ministers turning to one another, a ripple of murmuring heads.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You would like us to fight your rivals at your side.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: We prefer to be your trading partners rather than your enemies.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Partners.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Partners who once tried to break my spine.

panels.description: Revathi, seated beside Padmini, facing us now, not rising. Her voice is level and it carries.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And what do you offer for the men who died at Colachel and in Velinadu,

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: and in the smaller towns your patrols burned?

panels.description: The envoy hesitating, glancing down at the tricorne in his hands before he looks up.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: We cannot bring back the dead.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: We can only ensure that more do not die in similar misunderstandings.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off, small lettering)
copy.text: Misunderstandings. A pretty word for greed.

panels.description: The envoy again, his manner shifting to something almost casual. He turns the tricorne idly in his fingers and looks at no one.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: Not all houses on this coast share the Maharaja's... enthusiasm for consolidation.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: There are those who remember older arrangements. Older claims.

panels.description: One widescreen frame in depth, not split. Near foreground: Ramayyan's hand, the stylus stopped mid-stroke on the leaf. Mid-ground, at the left: Revathi's hand on her knee curling into a loose fist (gold armlet, indigo-and-gold sari border at the knee). Far end, raised on the platform: Varma's eyes narrowing (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He did not look at anyone in particular. He did not need to.

panels.description: Two-shot down the length of the hall: the envoy near, his back half to us; Varma far and small on the platform. The whole room silent between them.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: If the company wished, we could simply wait. Support those who feel aggrieved. Let internal divisions do what external force could not.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You will find the cost higher than you expect.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: Perhaps. We have learned patience.

panels.description: Bottom strip. Nagoji close, lamp-lit, his eyes gone somewhere else: black topknot, NO turban, first touch of grey at the temples only (NOT the grey later-life figure on the sheet), thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth, the silver chain of office. A soft-edged inset beside his face: a single palm leaf from Ramayyan's register, seen at a raking angle, rows of incised marks too fine to read; the focus is a small notch cut at the leaf's edge.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere, someone the Dutch could use was waiting. A claim. A grievance. A kinswoman with long memories.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of the name I had seen in Ramayyan's register.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Elayadathu. The entry marked HIGH.

panels.description: Large panel, the upper half of the page. Varma (V13 varma-v1 face; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare-chested, cream and gold cloth, gold necklaces) very still on the platform, the spear upright beside him, lamp flames standing straight in the windless hall. Shot from low, over the envoys' shoulders, so the king fills the frame and the Dutch are dark shapes at its foot. At the king's right, Nagoji standing (black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin). A small inset at the lower left corner: Revathi's hand on her knee (gold armlet, indigo-and-gold sari border), the fist from 8.1 loosening.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have learned that your guns cannot keep us from killing your men.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You have learned that some of our houses, like Velinadu and Padmini's line, will not sign papers that erase their names.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: So you bring different papers. Clever.

panels.description: The envoy opening his mouth to speak. In the foreground, Varma's raised hand, palm out, stops him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I approve of cleverness. It makes life interesting.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do not mistake my approval for weakness.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We will not sign away our children's choices.

panels.description: Close on Varma (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). Behind him, soft focus, Ramayyan's stylus paused over the leaf, his eyes lifted to the king.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you wish pepper, you will pay.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you wish warriors, you will not have them. This army is not for hire.

panels.description: Varma's gaze moving off the envoy toward the edge of the hall. The envoy's throat working.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: As for Captain De Lannoy, he is now my officer. He will not return to your service.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: We had hoped he might be returned as part of an exchange...

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width. Lannoy (tall, pale hair tied back, no wig, WHITE cotton coat, cloth-wrapped sword hilt) standing very straight at his pillar, eyes fixed somewhere past the envoys' shoulders.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You had hoped many things.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Hopes are not terms.

panels.description: Wide enough to hold the cause and the reaction in one frame. Ramayyan seated low at the foot of the platform, mild, a hint of something like kindness in his face. The two envoys standing before him: the younger (brown coat, his own hair, no wig) looks as if he might choke; the senior (grey powdered wig, charcoal coat) holds his features still by will alone. At frame right, at his pillar, Lannoy (WHITE cotton coat, pale hair tied back) listening, very straight.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If you wish to send him letters, we will read them first.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If they instruct him to betray his new oath, we will burn them without troubling him.

panels.description: Two-shot, the envoy standing, Ramayyan seated below him and entirely unbothered by it. Ramayyan has at last taken the Dutch document and laid it flat on the mat beside his own palm leaf, the two side by side in frame between them; the paper's lines are faint marks with no legible writing.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: May we sign the articles on trade and recognition?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: We will draft our own version. Your paper will be weighed against it. When both sides match, we will sign.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: How long will this take?

panels.description: Ramayyan close, already writing again on his leaf, the Dutch paper pinned under his elbow at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: As long as needed. We have learned to be patient.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: We will sign this truce at Mannar now.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: But the real treaty, the one where you promise never to stand in our way again, will come at Mavelikkara, when we are finished with the north.

panels.description: Wide. Later: the hall thinning, chiefs drifting away in muttering pairs, Nair palace guards (bare-chested, white mundu, sword and round shield) escorting the Dutch party toward the doors. Lannoy near a pillar at frame right, hands clasped behind his back. The senior envoy has paused beside him at frame left.

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: <You have chosen the wrong side. The company does not forget those who betray it.>

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: <It forgets those who die for it.>

panels.description: Close two-shot, both in profile, neither looking at the other. Frame left: the senior envoy, grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, thin lace at the cuff. Frame right: Lannoy, his own pale hair tied back, no wig, WHITE cotton coat, the cloth-wrapped sword hilt at his hip.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: <I prefer to be remembered by someone closer than Amsterdam.>

copy.speaker: SENIOR ENVOY
copy.text: <They call you traitor in Batavia.>

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: <Here, they call me kapitan. That is enough.>

panels.description: Wide. A long verandah outside the hall, carved wooden posts, palms and then the sea beyond, late afternoon light. Revathi at the edge, facing the water. Nagoji coming along the verandah behind her, the chain catching the light: BLACK hair in a Kerala topknot with only a first touch of grey at the temples (NOT the grey later-life figure on the sheet), NO turban, plain cream mundu with NO gold border and a shoulder cloth, the ivory-handled knife with the conch mark at his waist, the silver chain of office on his chest, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Satisfied?

panels.description: Revathi half-turned toward him (and toward us; he is off panel), the flat coins at her throat turned to small, steady suns by the low sun.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: They bowed. That is something.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But I have seen enough paper to know that men who sign today can tear tomorrow.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Ram will keep copies.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Paper burns. Land remembers.

panels.description: Nagoji's point of view, tight on the flat coins at her throat, catching the light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment I imagined that glint across a courtyard that smelled of rice and lamp smoke, not ink and powder.

panels.description: Padmini arriving along the verandah, her stick ticking on the boards. The three of them together against the sea. Nagoji: black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Today, my son, we have made them pay to do what they once did for free. That is a small victory.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Small victories add up.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: So do small betrayals.

panels.description: Tight insert, low in the frame. Revathi's hand, gold bangles at the wrist, brushing the back of Nagoji's LEFT hand (ridged, discoloured nails, the brand just above the wrist) as she turns toward the sea. Only the two hands and a fold of indigo sari.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It might have been an accident.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My pulse did not think so.

panels.description: Revathi turning from the rail to look straight at him, and at us, the bright sea behind her. He is off panel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She had dropped the titles she used in public.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Remember this, Nagoji. You are of this house now.

panels.description: Two-shot at the verandah rail, Revathi and Nagoji (black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin). Padmini a little way off, watching the two of them and pretending not to.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Few will talk of the quiet days after Colachel, when men in coats tried to rebuild their power with ink. Those days matter too.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will remember.

panels.description: Close on Revathi. Nagoji's shoulder and black topknot soft in the near foreground (cream shoulder cloth, silver chain, no turban).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Good. Because one day, when you are old and some young rider asks you how we kept this coast from becoming another Goa, you must tell him about both.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The charge and the papers. The dead on the sand and the men who bowed here today.

panels.description: Night. Nagoji's room. Nagoji cross-legged at a low writing board: black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, the silver chain of office still on his chest, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin. A clay oil lamp, a reed pen (kalam) and a small brass ink pot, a few sheets of paper angled away from us so only faint strokes show. His shadow large on the wall.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her words settled into me like stones in a pouch.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had learned from watching Ramayyan that paper, in the right hands, could be a weapon.

panels.description: The doorway. A guard's knuckles against the frame (a Nair palace guard, bare-chested, white mundu). In the foreground, the lamp: its oil not yet half gone.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Ramayyan requests you.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: Now.

panels.description: Wide. Ramayyan's room by lamplight, palm leaves everywhere. Ramayyan in the near foreground, bent over his leaf and not looking up, as if the day had never ended. Beyond him, Ibrahim Marakkar (shorter than the fishermen but broader; white turban; short grey-flecked beard; scar from his ANATOMICAL left ear to the jaw; dark short coat with bulging pockets over a pale vest and white mundu) half-risen from a low stool, a cup of buttermilk in his hand, his low talk cut off. In the doorway, Nagoji: black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, ivory knife, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Dutch?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Not Dutch. North.

panels.description: Ibrahim seated again, holding Nagoji's eyes (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat). The scar on his ANATOMICAL left side, ear to jaw, is turned to the lamp and to us, thrown into relief. Nagoji's shoulder and black topknot soft in the near foreground.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: My cousins trade in Maratha ports. Pune has heard of Colachel.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Some say a kingdom that can break a company square might one day threaten Maratha borders.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Others say it might make a useful ally against the English.

panels.description: Ibrahim standing by the lamp, his cup set down on the stool, answering (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat, the scar on his ANATOMICAL left side). Behind him, the open door and the night.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And which way does the wind blow?

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The wind blows in circles. It carries your name north and the Peshwa's name south.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Somewhere in the middle, men are deciding whether those names should be written in treaties or in obituaries.

panels.description: The doorway, empty now, the night beyond; the cup left on the stool. Nagoji looking at it (black topknot, NO turban, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin). Ramayyan at his leaf, the stylus paused. A small inset at the lower corner: Ramayyan's hand, the stylus moving again on the leaf, incised marks too fine to read.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You trust him?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: I trust his web. Every strand vibrates when something moves. If he lies to me, another strand will tell me.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: When the first letter comes, bring it to me.

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width. Night. Nagoji alone at his open window, seen from behind (black topknot, NO turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain), his lamp in the foreground behind him. The window faces inland: a dark line of hills under stars on the horizon. Palm fronds outside stream toward the window and toward us, and the lamp flame is bent back into the room, away from the window. A faint haze of dust hangs in the air.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Dutch had come bowing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It did not mean they had forgotten how to bite.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I could taste dust on the wind, dry and far away, carrying the Deccan toward this coast.
